findings.detail: The proposed views are Bernoulli feature masking of precomputed embedding coordinates, rather than independently dropout-corrupted versions of the item's metadata text encoded by the text encoder. This changes the uncertainty being estimated and the intervention being optimized; the code itself acknowledges that metadata text is absent.
findings.reproduction: For an item with text metadata and its precomputed vector batch, execute the view construction at lines 308-310: the text encoder is never called and only embedding dimensions are masked. Thus changing metadata while holding the stored embedding fixed has no effect on the views or agreement loss.
findings.correction: Construct M independent text-level metadata dropout views using the frozen text encoder during training and compute mu/variance from those encodings, or explicitly revise the requested mechanism/specification to embedding-coordinate dropout.

findings.detail: The real trainer's codebook initialization calls scikit-learn KMeans with n_init='auto'. On scikit-learn versions whose KMeans.fit does not accept/resolve this newer parameter, trainer startup fails before the first training step. The included migrated training log reports this exact failure (TypeError comparing n_init string with integer).
findings.reproduction: Run the trainer in an environment with scikit-learn 1.1.x: main reaches raw_module.init_codebook at train_rqvae.py:286, then KMeans(..., n_init='auto').fit(...) raises TypeError: '<=' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int'.
findings.correction: Use a compatible integer n_init (for example n_init=10), or pin and enforce a scikit-learn version that supports n_init='auto'; then rerun the actual trainer entry point.

findings.detail: The trainer defaults to the full stage1 embedding matrix and selects training items using only unique target IDs from train.parquet. That is not demonstrably a frozen train-only metadata/item-record data path: full-catalog embeddings are used for codebook initialization only on train_ids but also for validation collision measurement and final SID export. The required available training metadata views are absent from this path.
findings.reproduction: Inspect a run with a held-out item ID: it is included in all_embeddings and gets an exported SID at lines 415-427 despite not appearing in train_ids. No train-split metadata text is loaded anywhere in the trainer.
findings.correction: Keep held-out/catalog-wide rows out of training and uncertainty-view generation, document/verify the frozen split and row-to-item mapping, and use the frozen metadata source for training views. Full-catalog SID export may remain after fitting, provided it is inference-only and index-aligned.
